svg.aria-label: Fragmenta's engine blastfrag moved from a git-tag pin to a PyPI release and every published number stayed identical; the day before, a version bump done by substitution had rewritten the version field inside thirty-four committed artifacts, which were regenerated under the pinned engine; the product's headline remains a negative result under leave-one-site-out
svg.text: blastfrag on PyPI, and Fragmenta's numbers did not move
the engine pin changes from a git tag to a published release; the artifacts are the test
0.04.004 (morning)
blastfrag @ git tag v0.02.002
artifacts regenerated under the pinned
engine after a bump by substitution had
rewritten app_version in 34 of them
0.04.005 (afternoon)
blastfrag==0.2.2 from PyPI
trusted publisher, own repository;
the product declares no package and a
guard fails if a [project] table appears
DIFF OF THE ARTIFACTS
identical
every published number, all
sixteen cases; the bake gate
re-reads and re-hashes what it wrote
The headline the product exists to report has not changed either
leave-one-site-out, variance explained: xgboost -0.034 null model -0.216 (a 0.182 margin between two failures)
fixed-coefficient arms on an unseen site: published regression 0.802 Kuznetsov 0.311 (the only two positive)
kill criterion, written before the run: a positive score AND a 0.10 margin. It fired. The learned arms are not skill.
Reproducibility, stated precisely: byte-identical within an environment; better than 3e-08 relative across operating systems, because
two builds of the same pinned numpy reduce a dot product in a different order and no pin removes that. Both halves are gated in CI.
A pin is a claim about numbers. Change the pin, re-bake, diff the artifacts, then say "identical" only because the diff said so.
